description: Learners are introduced to a system of coordinates as a structured framework that uses numbers to describe exact locations, traced from the grid-planned streets of the Sindhu-Sarasvati Civilisation through Baudhayana, Aryabhata and Brahmagupta to the modern four-quadrant plane.

Learners follow Shalini guiding Reiaan around a new home on a rectangular pin grid, and learn to describe any location by counting units along two perpendicular directions. This builds the intuition of an ordered pair before the formal axes are introduced.

Learners set up the x-axis, y-axis and origin, and use the sign conventions to plot and read a point (x, y) as its perpendicular distances from the two axes. They also identify the four quadrants and the sign pattern of the coordinates in each.

topic: 1.4 Distance between two points in the 2-D plane
description: Learners find the distance between two points that lie on an axis or on a segment parallel to an axis, and then apply the Baudhayana-Pythagoras theorem to derive the distance between any two points in the xy-plane.
